summary: This document provides a YANG data model for the routing and wavelength assignment topology in Wavelength Switched Optical Networks (WSONs). It conforms to the Network Management Datastore Architecture (NMDA).

eli5.summary: In a light-based network, each message needs a color of light chosen for it. This document defines the data form for describing those networks and which colors are available.

questions: what is a yang data model for wson
what is a wavelength switched optical network
subtitle: A YANG module that describes wavelength-switched optical networks so controllers can read and configure their topology.

tldr.problem: Transparent Wavelength Switched Optical Networks (WSONs) assign a wavelength to each connection, and controllers need a standard, machine-readable way to describe the topology and the wavelength constraints.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines one YANG module, ietf-wson-topology, that augments the generic TE topology model (RFC 8795) with a WSON network type, a reconfigurable-node flag and DWDM or CWDM wavelength label information.
tldr.outcome: Nodes and controllers can share a WSON routing and wavelength assignment topology over NETCONF or RESTCONF. Impairment-aware and flexi-grid networks are out of scope.

today: RFC 9094 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2021, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What the Model Describes
sections.content:
RFC 9094 provides a YANG data model for the routing and wavelength assignment (RWA) Traffic Engineering (TE) topology in transparent Wavelength Switched Optical Networks (WSONs). It is a WSON-specific model built on the information model of RFC 7446 and on the two encoding documents, RFC 7581 and RFC 7579.

The model refers to the standard application mode of ITU-T G.698.2, which covers amplified multichannel dense wavelength division multiplexing with single-channel optical interfaces.

The RFC lists several uses. Nodes can capture their view of the overall WSON topology and expose it to a controller, and a controller can pass the topology on to other controllers. The model is used over NETCONF or RESTCONF and conforms to the Network Management Datastore Architecture (RFC 8342).
sections.eli5: It is a standard way for computers to write down a map of a network where every message rides on its own color of light, so other computers can read the map.

sections.title: What Is Out of Scope
sections.content:
Several related topics are explicitly left to other documents. Impairment-aware optical networks and flexi-grid networks are not covered here; the RFC points to separate drafts for the impairment-aware topology model and the flexi-grid topology model (both listed as work in progress). Transponder models and resource block models (for example 3R) are also out of scope.

The terms client, server, augment, data model and data node come from RFC 7950, and configuration data and state data come from RFC 6241. The RFC does not redefine them.
sections.eli5: This map only covers the simple kind of light network. Fancier kinds, and the boxes that make the light in the first place, are described somewhere else.

sections.title: How the Module Fits the TE Topology Models
sections.content:
The single module, ietf-wson-topology, augments the generic TE topology specification (RFC 8795). It imports ietf-network and ietf-network-topology (RFC 8345), ietf-te-topology (RFC 8795) and ietf-layer0-types (RFC 9093).

Data nodes use the standard prefixes of the modules they come from: l0-types, wsont, nw, nt and tet. The tree diagram in the RFC follows the notation of RFC 8340.
sections.eli5: The new module is an add-on to a general network-map form. It borrows most of its pieces from forms that already exist and only adds the parts about colors of light.

sections.title: The WSON Data Nodes
sections.content:
The module adds a wson-topology container under the TE topology network type. Its presence identifies a network as a WSON topology, and the other augmentations apply only to networks of that type.

For nodes it adds a wson-node container with a boolean leaf is-reconfigurable-node, which defaults to true. True means the node is a Reconfigurable Optical Add/Drop Multiplexer (ROADM); false means it is a Fixed Optical Add/Drop Multiplexer (FOADM).

The label restriction entries get a grid-type identityref and a priority leaf. The remaining augmentations add WSON cases to TE label start, end, step and hop, using groupings from ietf-layer0-types (l0-label-range-info, wson-label-start-end, wson-label-step and wson-label-hop). Labels are expressed as DWDM or CWDM channel numbers, and a hop on a DWDM path can be a single channel or a set of subcarrier channels. The same augmentations appear for configuration data, for the read-only information source entries, and for link templates.
sections.eli5: The form gets a box that says this is a light network, a yes/no question about whether a box in the network can change its colors, and lists of which colors are allowed where.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The module is accessed through NETCONF or RESTCONF. NETCONF's mandatory-to-implement secure transport is SSH, and RESTCONF's is TLS over HTTPS. The NETCONF access control model (RFC 8341) can restrict users to a subset of operations and content.

Writable data nodes (config true, the default) may be sensitive, and writing them without protection, for example with edit-config, can harm network operations. Readable nodes may also be sensitive, so read access should be controlled. The considerations in Section 8 of RFC 8795 apply, and the security considerations of the modules this one augments apply to the new data nodes.
sections.eli5: Anyone who can edit the map could break the network, and some parts of the map are private. So only trusted people should be allowed to read or change it, over secure connections.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA assigned the URI urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-wson-topology in the IETF XML Registry, with the IESG as registrant, and registered the module in the YANG Module Names registry with prefix wsont and reference RFC 9094. The module revision in the RFC is 2021-08-13, described as the initial version.
sections.eli5: The module was given its own official name tag in a public list, so nobody else uses the same one.
